name: Sprint System
description: A clean hold-to-sprint controller with configurable speed and smooth transitions.
details: A client-side sprint controller that responds to keyboard input, eases between movement speeds, and restores the default speed when the key is released.
instructions: In Roblox Studio, navigate to StarterPlayer > StarterPlayerScripts.
Insert a LocalScript and name it Sprint.
Copy the provided sprint system code into the LocalScript.
Adjust the WalkSpeed and SprintSpeed settings in the CONFIGURATION section to suit your game.
Set EnableTrails to true or false to enable or disable the sprint visual effects.
Press Play to test sprinting using Left Shift, the controller's left stick button (L3), or the mobile sprint button.
notes: Input uses Left Shift by default.

explanation.title: Understanding Sprint
explanation.intro: Learn how the LocalScript configures sprinting, changes walking speed smoothly, and binds sprint controls for different devices.

sections.title: Getting the player controls
sections.description: Players identifies the local player whose character will sprint. ContextActionService binds a named action to keyboard, controller, and Roblox's touch button. TweenService smooths speed changes, while RunService updates the visual effects as the player moves.
sections.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Player = Players.LocalPlayer
sections.note: The LocalPlayer property is available to LocalScripts running for a player.

sections.title: Choosing speeds and effects
sections.description: Config groups the settings the developer can customise. WalkSpeed is the normal speed, SprintSpeed is used while sprinting, and TransitionTime sets how long the change takes. The remaining values control trails and particles.
sections.code:
-- CONFIGURATION
local Config = {
	WalkSpeed = 16, -- Normal movement speed
	SprintSpeed = 50, -- Movement speed while sprinting
	TransitionTime = 0.2, -- Time taken to transition between speeds
sections.note: Adjust these values to fit the pace of your game.

sections.title: Changing speed smoothly
sections.description: SetSprint first checks that a living Humanoid is ready. It cancels an earlier speed tween if needed, chooses the target speed based on enabled, then creates and plays a new tween to change WalkSpeed over the configured time.
sections.code:
local function SetSprint(enabled)
	if not CurrentHumanoid or CurrentHumanoid.Health <= 0 then
		return
	end

	IsSprinting = enabled

	if SpeedTween then
		SpeedTween:Cancel()
	end

	local targetSpeed = enabled and Config.SprintSpeed or Config.WalkSpeed
sections.note: Using the same function for start and stop keeps the speed logic in one place.

sections.title: Responding to button presses
sections.description: HandleSprint receives the input state for the sprint action. Begin starts sprinting; End or Cancel stops it. Returning Sink tells Roblox this action handled the input.
sections.code:
local function HandleSprint(_, inputState)
	if inputState == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then
		SetSprint(true)
	elseif inputState == Enum.UserInputState.End
		or inputState == Enum.UserInputState.Cancel then
		SetSprint(false)
	end

	return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
end
sections.note: Cancel also handles cases where the input ends unexpectedly.

sections.title: Setting up each character and controls
sections.description: SetupCharacter waits for the new Humanoid, restores normal speed, clears the previous sprint state, and creates its effects. CharacterAdded runs that setup after respawn. BindAction registers keyboard and controller inputs and enables a touch button with a title and screen position.
sections.code:
Player.CharacterAdded:Connect(SetupCharacter)

if Player.Character then
	SetupCharacter(Player.Character)
end

ContextActionService:BindAction(
	"Sprint",
	HandleSprint,
	true,
	Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift,
	Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3
)
sections.note: The third BindAction argument enables Roblox's on-screen button for touch devices.
